prompt:
Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Sam, the dog detective (a big brown dog in a light blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped dark blue tie and a blue-gray fedora). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: animation 7 (a separate part the game draws on top of the body, such as the head), facing right (6 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 36 to 204 pixels tall and from 224 to 732 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig047_04/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.

SOURCE-VERIFIED SINGLE EFFECT CEL CORRECTION: Generic multiple-frames/Sam/start/facing-right content above does NOT describe image1. This call contains EXACTLY ONE WHOLE EFFECT drawing,source costume047_1805,shown8x (1408x320) in the center. The firstimage is the only CONTENT reference;image2 is approved stroke style only. NO CHARACTER,NO DOG,NO RABBIT,NO HAND,NO HEAD,NO WEAPON,NO SCENE. Do not paint the character from image2. Output1536x1024,one whole effect at the SAME1408x320 size and internal placement shown in image1.
This is a brief comic projectile trail and wood-impact effect from the hallway outside Flint Paper's office. Precisely preserve the direction,slight bends,small gaps and relative positions of every component: ONE very thin long WHITE motion trace sloping gently down right from a tiny dark gray projectile tip on its far left to a SMALL dark brown impact around the middle-right;THREE detached small white trail pieces continuing towards the right;ONE separate short bottom-right white trail with its actual little dark gray tip on the left. Keep all tiny DARK BROWN #532b00 splinters and specks at the impact. The drawing is mostly empty transparent space. White traces are about one original pixel thick (8pixels shown here),not broad tapered spears. Smooth the source pixel steps gently while keeping the original narrow envelope and bends. Do not turn all white pieces into one connected line. Do not add tips to the detached middle white pieces. Brown impacts remain tiny thin irregular slivers,not a big cloud,star,flame,smoke,golden burst,door or scene. Keep original flat white/gray/dark brown palette,no gradients,no laser glow,no haze,no shadow. Actual transparent RGBA around and between every small piece. Do not crop any tip or speck at the canvas edges. No labels,IDs,text,grid or borders.
